# WAF Threat Hunt — CloudFront EEXAMPLE000001 / WebACL CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4
**Window:** 2026-10-10 17:00:00.000 → 18:15:00.000 UTC (75 min) · **Source:** `aws-waf-logs-012345678901_1` (Athena, account 012345678901_1, us-east-1)

> **⚠️ Data-note (must read):** The epoch-ms bounds in the assignment (`1760115600000`/`1760120100000`) resolve to **2025**-10-10, but the actual WAF data under the `2026/10/10/` prefix carries timestamps `1791651600044`–`1791656099333` = **2026**-10-10 17:00–18:15 UTC. The assignment's epoch constants were off by exactly one year. I used the correct 2026 bounds **[1791651600000, 1791656100000)**, which match the folder path and the stated calendar window. All 169,927 records fall inside the window.

---

## 1. Overall volume & action breakdown

| Action | Count | % |
|---|---|---|
| **ALLOW** | 169,677 | 99.853% |
| **BLOCK** | 250 | 0.147% |
| CHALLENGE / CAPTCHA / COUNT (terminating) | 0 | 0% |

Per-5-min buckets (UTC):

| Bucket | ALLOW | BLOCK |

Traffic is a **flat high plateau (~11k req / 5 min)** from the very first bucket — not a ramp. The baseline flood was already saturating at 17:00. Blocks cluster in **17:00–17:10 (225 of 250)** (the enumeration + sqlmap scans) with a small tail 17:45–18:00. **Method split: GET 126,105 / POST 43,822.**

> **🚩 Rate-rule gap, confirmed:** `AWS-RateBasedRule-IP-300-CreatedByCloudFront` evaluated all 169,927 requests (maxRateAllowed=300) but is **COUNT-only → 0 blocks**. The dominant IP ran ~11,000 req/5min — **~37× the 300 limit** — in **every** bucket and was never throttled.

---

## 2. What was STOPPED (250 BLOCK, 0 CHALLENGE/CAPTCHA)

| terminatingRuleId | Type | Count |
|---|---|---|
| AWS-AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet | MANAGED_RULE_GROUP | 245 |
| AWS-AWSManagedRulesKnownBadInputsRuleSet | MANAGED_RULE_GROUP | 5 |

Matched sub-rules (labels on blocked requests):
- **core-rule-set:BadBots_Header** — 225 (the entire **sqlmap** campaign; blocked on UA)
- **core-rule-set:RestrictedExtensions_URIPath** — 15 (`/.env`, `/.env.bak`, `/web.config`, `/wp-config.php.bak`, `/.aws/credentials`)
- **core-rule-set:GenericLFI_URIPath** — 5
- **known-bad-inputs:ExploitablePaths_URIPath** — 5

Example blocked requests: `GET /catalog` (sqlmap UA, BadBots_Header); `GET /.env`, `GET /.aws/credentials`, `GET /web.config`, `GET /wp-config.php.bak`, `GET /dev/.env`, `GET /backup/.aws/credentials` (RestrictedExtensions/ExploitablePaths). **Nothing was blocked by AntiDDoS (p0), IpReputation (p2), or SQLiRuleSet (p5).**

---

## 3. What GOT THROUGH (allowed but malicious)

**No managed-rule attack signature leaked through as a COUNT-only ALLOW.** The only label on ALLOW traffic is `awswaf:managed:aws:anti-ddos:challengeable-request` (125,855). CRS/KnownBadInputs attack labels appear **exclusively on BLOCK** records, and a URI/args scan for SQLi/XSS/`../`/`${jndi:}` returned **15 hits, all BLOCKED (0 allowed)**. So injection payloads did **not** reach the origin.

What *did* get through to the EKS ALB origin is malicious by **behavior**, evading WAF because the rate rule is COUNT-only and the content is signature-clean:

1. **Checkout/payment flood & card-testing — 198.51.100.10, 168,126 req, 100% ALLOWED.** UA `Artillery (https://artillery.io)` (load-test tool). Hammered `/checkout` (18,512), `/checkout/payment` (9,262 POST), `/checkout/delivery` (9,260), `/cart` (23,922 GET + 14,678 POST). ~37× rate limit, never throttled.
2. **Card-testing burst — 198.51.100.30, 1,351 req, 100% ALLOWED.** **1,350 POSTs to `/checkout/payment`** in a single 18:05 burst, normal Chrome UA → textbook card-testing, straight to origin (also >300/5min, not rate-blocked).
3. **Sensitive-path enumeration — 198.51.100.20, 200 of 225 ALLOWED.** Scanner reached origin on `/.git/config`, `/.git/HEAD`, `/.ssh/id_rsa`, `/actuator/health`, `/actuator/env`, `/actuator/heapdump`, `/swagger-ui.html`, `/v2/api-docs`, `/phpmyadmin/`, `/adminer.php`, `/dump.sql`, `/backup.sql`, `/site.tar.gz`, `/server-status`, `/elmah.axd`, `/login.jsp`, `/manager/html` (plus `/dev/`, `/old/`, `/test/`, `/backup/` prefixes). Only 25 of its probes (the `.env`/`.aws/credentials`/`web.config`/`wp-config.php.bak` set) were blocked.

---

## 4. Attacker profiling

**Only 4 source IPs in the entire window (all US):**

| clientIp | Country | Total | ALLOW | BLOCK | Profile |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **198.51.100.10** | US | 168,126 (98.9%) | 168,126 | 0 | Artillery flood → checkout/payment/cart |
| **198.51.100.30** | US | 1,351 | 1,351 | 0 | Card-testing burst (1,350 POST /checkout/payment @ 18:05) |
| **198.51.100.20** | US | 225 | 200 | 25 | Sensitive-path / secret-file scanner |
| **198.51.100.60** | US | 225 | 0 | 225 | **sqlmap** SQLi scanner (fully blocked) |

**User-agents (scanner/tool UAs flagged):**
- `Artillery (https://artillery.io)` — 168,126 (load-test tool) 🚩
- `sqlmap/1.8.2#stable` — 225 (SQLi scanner) 🚩 → **all BLOCKED**
- Chrome/141 — 1,351 (198.51.100.30, card-testing) + 225 (198.51.100.20, scanner masquerading as Chrome)

**Top URIs:** `/cart` (GET 23,922 + POST 14,678), `/catalog` (20,508), `/home` (20,498), `/checkout` (18,513), `/checkout/payment` (POST 9,262+1,350), `/checkout/delivery` (9,260), plus ~8 `/catalog/<uuid>` product pages (4k–8k each). **Methods:** GET 126,105 / POST 43,822.

---

## 5. Attack taxonomy (injection / scan / card-testing)

**Injection — BLOCKED (0 reached origin).**
- SQLi: 225 req from **198.51.100.60** (sqlmap/1.8.2) → **100% BLOCKED** by CRS BadBots_Header on the sqlmap UA. SQLiRuleSet (p5) itself fired zero terminations (UA block was first).
- LFI / path-traversal / known-bad-inputs: 15 URI/args hits (`../`, GenericLFI, ExploitablePaths) + credential/config-file probes → **all 15 BLOCKED** (GenericLFI_URIPath 5, RestrictedExtensions 15, ExploitablePaths 5).
- XSS / command-injection / `${jndi:}` / SSRF: **none observed.**

**Scanning / enumeration — MOSTLY ALLOWED.** Source **198.51.100.20** (225 req, 200 allowed / 25 blocked), ~200 distinct sensitive paths, 1 req each, Chrome-spoofed UA. **Allowed to origin:** `/.git/config`, `/.ssh/id_rsa`, `/actuator/env`, `/actuator/heapdump`, `/swagger-ui.html`, `/v2/api-docs`, `/phpmyadmin/`, `/dump.sql`, `/backup.sql`, `/site.tar.gz`, `/server-status`, `/wp-login.php`, `/admin`, `/login.jsp`. **Blocked:** only `/.env`, `/.env.bak`, `/.aws/credentials`, `/web.config`, `/wp-config.php.bak` (and prefixed variants) = 25.

**Card-testing — ALLOWED (the core exposure).** Repeated POSTs to payment/checkout/cart at high rate, straight to the EKS ALB origin:
- **198.51.100.10** (Artillery): 9,262 POST `/checkout/payment`, 18,512 `/checkout`, 9,260 `/checkout/delivery`, 14,678 POST `/cart` — 100% ALLOWED, ~37× rate limit sustained for the full 75 min.
- **198.51.100.30**: 1,350 POST `/checkout/payment` in one 18:05 burst — 100% ALLOWED. (Request bodies not captured by WAF — `args` empty — but endpoint+volume+method pattern = card-testing.)

### Timeline
- **17:00** — Flood (198.51.100.10) already at full ~11k/5min; sqlmap (198.51.100.60) + path scanner (198.51.100.20) active → block spike 17:00–17:10 (225 blocks).
- **17:15–18:00** — Flood continues flat; only a small block tail (25) 17:45–18:00.
- **18:05** — **Card-testing burst**: 198.51.100.30 fires 1,350 POST `/checkout/payment`, all allowed.
- **18:10** — Flood still running (11,743) at window close.

### Blocked-vs-allowed verdict (core of the hunt)
| Category | Blocked | Allowed to origin |
|---|---|---|
| SQLi (sqlmap) | 225 (100%) | 0 |
| LFI / traversal / bad-input payloads | 15 (100%) | 0 |
| Secret/config-file probes | 25 | — |
| Other sensitive-path enumeration | — | ~200 |
| Checkout/payment/cart flood (Artillery) | 0 | 168,126 |
| Card-testing burst (POST /checkout/payment) | 0 | 1,350 |

**Bottom line:** WAF reliably stopped signature-based attacks (SQLi scanner, injection payloads, secret-file names) — 250 blocks, 0 leaks. But the **high-volume behavioral abuse — the 168k-request Artillery flood against checkout/payment and the 1,350-POST card-testing burst — passed 100% through to the EKS origin solely because the rate-based rule is COUNT-only.** Switching p1 `AWS-RateBasedRule-IP-300` from COUNT to BLOCK (and/or adding a checkout-specific rate rule) would have throttled all three high-volume IPs. Secondarily, the enumeration scanner (198.51.100.20) reached the origin on ~200 sensitive paths that CRS did not match — worth a custom path-block rule for `.git`/`.ssh`/`actuator`/`swagger`/`phpmyadmin`.

# Findings: Origin-Side Outcome for Allowed-Malicious Traffic

## Bottom line
**I could NOT determine the origin-side HTTP outcomes.** Every data source that records origin/application response codes is either disabled, access-denied, or holds no data for the incident window. This is itself a significant **visibility/investigation gap**: the account cannot currently prove whether the card-testing POSTs were processed or whether any sensitive-path probe returned a body. Below is exactly what I found and what is missing.

## Task 1 — ALB discovery (with a critical discrepancy)
- The CloudFront origin DNS in the brief is `k8s-ui-ui-0000000001.elb.us-west-2.amazonaws.com` and is described as an **ALB**.
- The **only** load balancer in account `012345678901_1` / `us-west-2` is:
  - Name: `k8s-ui-ui-0000000002`
  - ARN: `[redacted ARN]`
  - Type: **network (NLB)** — not an ALB
  - Scheme: `internet-facing`, State: `active`
  - DNS: `k8s-ui-ui-0000000003.elb.us-west-2.amazonaws.com`
- **Two discrepancies vs the brief:** (a) the DNS hash differs (`deed3f1375016a93` ≠ `235939453c7ba3a0`), and (b) it is an **NLB, not an ALB**. The named origin may have been replaced/recreated (hash changed), or the exact origin LB no longer exists. The current `k8s-ui-ui-0000000002` NLB is almost certainly the live `ui` ingress origin (same k8s-generated name), but I cannot positively confirm it is the exact CloudFront origin.
- **Consequence for the investigation:** An **NLB operates at L4 and does NOT log HTTP `elb_status_code` / `target_status_code`** even when access logs are enabled. So the ALB-access-log analysis requested in Task 3 (status-code and sent_bytes distributions per path) is **not obtainable from this load balancer regardless of logging configuration.**

## Task 2 — Access logging
- `describe_load_balancer_attributes`: **`access_logs.s3.enabled = false`**, bucket empty, prefix empty.
- No ELB/ALB log S3 bucket exists (bucket list shows only CloudTrail, WAF, CloudFront, CUR, Athena-results, KB buckets).
- **ALB/NLB access logs are NOT enabled → no origin status codes available this way.** (And as noted, an NLB wouldn't carry HTTP codes anyway.)

## Task 3 — Not possible (see Task 2). 

## Task 4 — Kubernetes / app fallback (also blocked)
- EKS cluster discovered: **`example-shop`** (ACTIVE, us-west-2).
- **kubectl access DENIED**: `the server has asked for the client to provide credentials` (cannot list namespaces, pods, or ingress; cannot read `ui` app or ingress-controller pod logs).
- EKS cluster logging (`/aws/eks/example-shop/cluster`) is enabled only for `api / audit / authenticator` (control-plane). `controllerManager`/`scheduler` disabled. **No application or ingress HTTP logs** are shipped — this group cannot yield response codes.
- **No Container Insights** application log groups exist (`/aws/containerinsights/*` empty).
- **Application Signals** (`/aws/application-signals/data`, 15 GB) exists and would carry HTTP server spans with status codes — but its **most recent event is 2026-04-10** (`1786320300000`), ~6 months before the incident. **Zero records in 2026-10-10 17:00–18:15 UTC.** Not usable.
- **Traffic generator** (`/ecs/example-shop-traffic-generator`): has data in the window and confirms the **Artillery** load generator was running (phases starting at 18:04/18:09 UTC — matches the "Artillery" UA from `198.51.100.10`), but it logs only test-run metadata (phase/user-rate/test-run-id). **No per-request HTTP status codes, no checkout/path/response info** (44 records in window; filter for `codes|status|checkout|payment|.git|actuator` returned 0 matches).
- **CloudFront access logs** (`example-shop-cf-logs-012345678901_1`) exist and — because POST `/checkout/*`, `/cart`, and the enumeration paths are uncacheable and proxied to origin — the edge `sc-status`/`sc-bytes` would be a reasonable proxy for origin outcome. **But listing/reading this bucket is IAM AccessDenied** (`s3:ListBucket` not permitted for the agent role).

## Direct answers to the two most important questions
1. **Did the card-testing POSTs (`198.51.100.10`, `198.51.100.30`) get processed (2xx/3xx) at the origin?** — **UNKNOWN / undeterminable** with available access. No ALB HTTP logs (disabled + NLB), no app pod logs (kubectl denied), no Application Signals data for the window, and CloudFront logs access-denied.
2. **Did any sensitive-path probe (`198.51.100.20`) return HTTP 200 with a body (secret exposure)?** — **UNKNOWN / undeterminable** for the same reasons. I cannot confirm or rule out exposure of `/.git/config`, `/.ssh/id_rsa`, `/actuator/env`, `/actuator/heapdump`, `/v2/api-docs`, `/dump.sql`, `/backup.sql`, `/server-status`, etc.

## What's missing (to close the gap)
To obtain origin outcomes, one of the following is needed:
- **Access to the CloudFront access logs** (grant the agent role `s3:ListBucket`/`s3:GetObject` on `example-shop-cf-logs-012345678901_1`, or run an Athena query over them) — this is the fastest path since those logs very likely already contain `sc-status` and `sc-bytes` for every proxied request in the window. *(This is CloudFront/edge domain — recommend the lead route it accordingly.)*
- **kubectl/EKS data-plane access** to `example-shop` to read `ui` and ingress-controller pod logs for 17:00–18:15 UTC.
- Forward-looking remediation: enable the `ui` application / ingress-controller access logs to CloudWatch (and note that the NLB cannot provide HTTP-layer logging — an ALB or app-level logging is required for L7 outcomes).

I recommend the lead agent engage the CloudFront/edge-logs owner and/or restore EKS data-plane access, since the root evidence lies in resources currently outside my reach.

# Threat hunt conclusion — CloudFront `d111111abcdef8.cloudfront.net` (EEXAMPLE000001), 2026-10-10 17:00–18:15 UTC

**Setup.** The distribution is protected by WAF Web ACL `CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4` (DefaultAction Allow). Origin is an internet-facing EKS NLB in us-west-2. CloudFront access logging (legacy field) is off, so **WAF logs in `aws-waf-logs-012345678901_1` are the authoritative edge record**. Time anchor verified: the data under `.../2026/10/10/17|18/` resolves to exactly the user's window (epoch 1791651600 = 2026-10-10 17:00:00 UTC). **169,927 requests from only 4 US source IPs** — a coordinated, non-organic pattern.

## What looks malicious (symptoms)
Three adversarial campaigns plus one high-volume flood, running concurrently from window start:
- **198.51.100.60** — `sqlmap/1.8.2` SQL-injection scanner (225 req).
- **198.51.100.20** — sensitive-path enumeration, ~200 distinct recon paths, Chrome-spoofed UA (225 req).
- **198.51.100.30** — **card-testing**: 1,350 POSTs to `/checkout/payment` in a single ~18:05 burst, normal Chrome UA.
- **198.51.100.10** — "Artillery" UA flooding `/checkout`, `/checkout/payment`, `/checkout/delivery`, `/cart` (168,126 req, ~99% of all traffic, ~37× the rate limit).

**Calibration (noteworthy observation):** the 198.51.100.10 "Artillery" flood correlates with the account's own `example-shop-traffic-generator` ECS service running Artillery during the window — so this IP is **likely in-house synthetic load**, not an external attacker. The genuinely adversarial signals are the sqlmap scan, the enumeration, and the card-testing burst.

## What was STOPPED (cause — WAF working as intended)
**250 blocks, 0 leaks of any signature-based attack.** Confirmed from the logs:
- Entire **sqlmap SQLi campaign (225)** blocked by `AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet` → `BadBots_Header` (matched on the sqlmap user-agent).
- **15 injection/LFI/traversal payloads** (GenericLFI, ExploitablePaths) and **25 secret-file-name probes** (`.env`, `.aws/credentials`, `web.config`, `wp-config.php.bak`) blocked by CommonRuleSet / KnownBadInputsRuleSet.
- Verified: all 15 URI/args injection indicators were BLOCK; **none were ALLOW**. No SQLi/XSS/JNDI payload reached the origin.

## What GOT THROUGH (cause + actionable root cause)
All high-volume **behavioral** abuse was allowed to the origin because it is signature-clean and WAF didn't rate-limit it:
- **168,126** Artillery flood requests (198.51.100.10) — 100% allowed.
- **1,350** card-testing POSTs to `/checkout/payment` (198.51.100.30) — 100% allowed.
- **~200** sensitive-path enumeration probes (198.51.100.20) allowed to origin: `/.git/config`, `/.git/HEAD`, `/.ssh/id_rsa`, `/actuator/env`, `/actuator/heapdump`, `/swagger-ui.html`, `/v2/api-docs`, `/phpmyadmin/`, `/dump.sql`, `/backup.sql`, `/site.tar.gz`, `/server-status`, `/wp-login.php`, `/admin`, etc. (only 25 of its probes were blocked).

**Root cause of "got through":** the priority-1 rate-based rule `AWS-RateBasedRule-IP-300-CreatedByCloudFront` is set to **Count, not Block** — confirmed directly in the Web ACL config (`Action: {Count:{}}`, limit 300/5min/IP). The dominant IP ran ~37× that limit in every 5-minute bucket and was never throttled. **Secondary cause:** no WAF rule covers sensitive-path enumeration, so the scanner's recon paths reached the origin. Both are actionable WAF hardening items, handed to the mitigation subagent (rate rule Count→Block, add a sensitive-path block rule, IP-set block of the adversarial IPs).

## Investigation gap (access-bounded, could not close)
WAF logs prove these requests were *allowed to* the origin, but **whether they succeeded there is undeterminable with current access**. Exhausted every outcome source: ALB/NLB access logs disabled (and the origin is an L4 NLB that can't log HTTP status), EKS `example-shop` kubectl denied, Application Signals has no data for the window (latest event ~2026-04-10), no CloudWatch Logs deliveries, and the `example-shop-cf-logs-012345678901_1` CloudFront-logs bucket is `s3:ListBucket` AccessDenied to the agent role. **Consequence:** I cannot confirm or rule out whether the card-testing POSTs were processed (2xx/3xx) or whether any enumeration probe (`/.git/config`, `/.ssh/id_rsa`, `/actuator/env`, `/dump.sql`, …) returned HTTP 200 with a body — i.e., a potential secret/data exposure. Closing this requires read access to the CloudFront logs bucket (or an Athena query over them) and/or restored EKS data-plane access. If exposure is later confirmed, follow-up mitigation (credential rotation, origin hardening) would be warranted — flagged to the mitigation subagent as a dependency.

**Bottom line:** WAF reliably stopped every signature-based attack (sqlmap SQLi, injection/traversal payloads, secret-file names) — 250 blocks, zero leaks. What got through was the high-volume behavioral abuse — the checkout/cart flood and the 1,350-request card-testing burst against `/checkout/payment`, plus ~200 recon paths — all because the rate-based rule is Count-only and no path rule exists. {"type": "investigation_gap", "id": "gap-origin-outcome", "title": "Origin outcome of allowed requests is unverifiable (and a scope discrepancy)", "description": "The origin-impact analysis exhausted every source that could show whether the ~169,477 allowed requests succeeded at the origin, and all are unavailable for the window:

- **Origin is an L4 NLB, not an ALB.** The only load balancer (k8s-ui-ui-0000000002, DNS hash deed3f1375016a93) is a Network Load Balancer whose DNS hash also differs from the CloudFront origin named in the brief (235939453c7ba3a0). NLBs do not log HTTP status codes even when access logs are on.
- **ALB/NLB access logs disabled** (access_logs.s3.enabled=false); no ELB log bucket exists.
- **kubectl access denied** on EKS cluster example-shop — ui and ingress-controller pod logs unreachable.
- **EKS logging is control-plane only** (api/audit/authenticator); no application/ingress HTTP logs, no Container Insights.
- **Application Signals stale** — /aws/application-signals/data last event 2026-04-10, ~6 months before the incident; zero records in-window.
- **CloudFront access logs access-denied** (s3:ListBucket on example-shop-cf-logs-012345678901_1) — these would be the fastest proxy for origin outcome and likely hold sc-status per request.

Consequence: cannot confirm or rule out whether the card-testing POSTs to /checkout/payment were processed (2xx/3xx) or whether any sensitive-path probe (/.git/config, /.ssh/id_rsa, /actuator/env, /actuator/heapdump, /dump.sql, etc.) returned a body. This bounds the confidence on true severity. To close: grant read on the CloudFront logs bucket (or Athena over it), restore EKS data-plane access, and enable L7 application/ingress access logging going forward."}

# Mitigation Summary

## Action
In a single update to the CloudFront WAF Web ACL CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4 (account 012345678901_1): (1) change the priority rate-based rule AWS-RateBasedRule-IP-300-CreatedByCloudFront from Count to Block; (2) add a custom URI-path regex rule to block sensitive-path enumeration; and (3) create a dedicated IP set + rule to immediately block the four known malicious IPs (198.51.100.10, 198.51.100.30, 198.51.100.20, 198.51.100.60). All existing managed rule groups are preserved.

## Reasoning
The threat hunt confirmed two latent WAF misconfigurations on the Web ACL fronting CloudFront EEXAMPLE000001: the priority-1 rate-based rule is Count-only (so the 168,126-request Artillery flood at ~37× the limit and the 1,350-POST card-testing burst passed 100% to origin), and no rule covers sensitive-path enumeration (so ~200 recon probes reached origin). This is forward-looking hardening of a latent misconfiguration, not a deployment rollback. The four implicated IPs are added to a dedicated block for immediate relief while the structural rules take effect.

# Investigation Summary

## Symptoms

### Malicious traffic reaching the EKS origin
**Description:** Over the 2026-10-10 17:00–18:15 UTC window, malicious traffic reached the EKS ingress ALB origin behind CloudFront EEXAMPLE000001: (1) a 168,126-request Artillery volumetric flood against checkout/cart (~37× the rate limit), (2) a 1,350-POST card-testing burst to /checkout/payment at 18:05, and (3) ~200 of 225 sensitive-path recon probes (.git, .ssh, actuator, swagger, dumps). Injection attacks did NOT reach origin — the sqlmap SQLi scanner was fully blocked and all 15 traversal/LFI payload matches were blocked.
**Time:** 2026-10-10T17:00:00Z - 2026-10-10T18:15:00Z

## Findings

### Cause: Rate-based rule is COUNT-only, letting a 37× flood through
**Description:** Source **198.51.100.10** (US) generated **168,126 requests (98.9% of all traffic)**, every one ALLOWED, 0 blocked. It sustained ~11,000 req per 5-min bucket in every bucket — ~37× over the P1 rate-based rule's 300/5-min limit. The traffic targets legitimate e-commerce endpoints with a card-testing / checkout-abuse signature: POST /checkout/payment (9,262), POST /cart (14,678), POST /checkout/delivery (9,260), POST /checkout (9,257), plus heavy GET /cart (23,922), /catalog (20,508), /home (20,498). It evaded WAF because the P1 rate-based rule is set to **COUNT only, not BLOCK** — all 169,927 req were evaluated at maxrate 300 but zero were blocked; had P1 been in BLOCK mode this flood would have been stopped.
**Cascades to:** symptom-malicious-through

### Cause: Sensitive-file/path scanning allowed through to origin
**Description:** Source **198.51.100.20** (US) ran 225 reconnaissance probes, **200 allowed / 25 blocked**, enumerating sensitive files and paths: /.ssh/id_rsa, /.git/config, /.aws/credentials, /wp-config.php.bak, /actuator/heapdump, /dump.sql, /.env.bak, /phpmyadmin/, /server-status, /swagger-ui.html, and many backup/VCS/actuator variants. The managed rule groups do not cover these paths, so 200 recon probes reached the EKS origin; only 25 were blocked (RestrictedExtensions_URIPath, GenericLFI_URIPath, KnownBadInputs ExploitablePaths_URIPath).
**Cascades to:** symptom-malicious-through

### Root Cause: WAF Web ACL mis-tuned: non-blocking rate rule + coverage gaps
**Description:** The Web ACL `CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4` defaults to **Allow** with its P1 rate-based rule in **COUNT mode** and managed rule groups that miss checkout-abuse and sensitive-path reconnaissance. This is the fundamental cause from which both campaigns' success cascades: the 37× checkout flood and the file-scanning both reached the origin because of this tuning. Correcting the WAF configuration (rate rule to BLOCK, add path-based blocks) stops recurrence.
**Cascades to:** finding-rate-count-only, finding-scanner-allowed

### Hypothesis: Injection/XSS/LFI did NOT breach
**Description:** A URI/args scan for SQLi/XSS/traversal (`union select`, `or 1=1`, `<script`, `../`, `${jndi:}`, `sleep(`) returned 15 hits — **all 15 BLOCKED, 0 reached origin**. The sqlmap SQLi scanner (198.51.100.60, 225 req) was fully blocked by CommonRuleSet BadBots_Header on the UA. No XSS, command-injection, JNDI, or SSRF payload was observed in args at all. Injection as a category was fully contained; the real exposure is volumetric/card-testing abuse and sensitive-path recon.
**Cascades to:** symptom-malicious-through

#### Gaps
- **Origin outcome of allowed requests is unverifiable (and a scope discrepancy):** The origin-impact analysis exhausted every source that could show whether the ~169,477 allowed requests succeeded at the origin, and all are unavailable for the window:

- **Origin is an L4 NLB, not an ALB.** The only load balancer (k8s-ui-ui-0000000002, DNS hash deed3f1375016a93) is a Network Load Balancer whose DNS hash also differs from the CloudFront origin named in the brief (235939453c7ba3a0). NLBs do not log HTTP status codes even when access logs are on.
- **ALB/NLB access logs disabled** (access_logs.s3.enabled=false); no ELB log bucket exists.
- **kubectl access denied** on EKS cluster example-shop — ui and ingress-controller pod logs unreachable.
- **EKS logging is control-plane only** (api/audit/authenticator); no application/ingress HTTP logs, no Container Insights.
- **Application Signals stale** — /aws/application-signals/data last event 2026-04-10, ~6 months before the incident; zero records in-window.
- **CloudFront access logs access-denied** (s3:ListBucket on example-shop-cf-logs-012345678901_1) — these would be the fastest proxy for origin outcome and likely hold sc-status per request.

Consequence: cannot confirm or rule out whether the card-testing POSTs to /checkout/payment were processed (2xx/3xx) or whether any sensitive-path probe (/.git/config, /.ssh/id_rsa, /actuator/env, /actuator/heapdump, /dump.sql, etc.) returned a body. This bounds the confidence on true severity. To close: grant read on the CloudFront logs bucket (or Athena over it), restore EKS data-plane access, and enable L7 application/ingress access logging going forward.
- **WAF logs stored in S3, not CloudWatch Logs:** WAF logging for `CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4` is delivered to S3 bucket `aws-waf-logs-012345678901_1` (not CloudWatch Logs), and CloudFront access logging is disabled. Pattern analysis will require querying the S3 WAF logs (e.g. via Athena) rather than Logs Insights; direct CloudWatch log querying is not available for this traffic.

Two refinements from the parallel origin-impact investigation — please fold these into your plan; no new root cause, but they change the IP-block action and leave one item explicitly out of scope:

1) ATTRIBUTION CAVEAT on one of the four IPs: 198.51.100.10 (the "Artillery" UA, 168,126-request checkout/cart flood) correlates with an IN-ACCOUNT ECS service `example-shop-traffic-generator` (log group /ecs/example-shop-traffic-generator) that was running Artillery load tests during the exact window (phases at 18:04/18:09 UTC). So 198.51.100.10 is very likely this account's OWN synthetic load generator, not an external adversary. Treat its inclusion in the immediate IP-set block as REQUIRING confirmation first — blocking it would kill the account's own load generator and may be undesirable. The genuinely adversarial IPs are 198.51.100.60 (sqlmap, already fully blocked by WAF), 198.51.100.20 (sensitive-path enumeration), and 198.51.100.30 (card-testing burst on /checkout/payment). Recommend splitting the IP block so 198.51.100.20 and 198.51.100.30 are blocked immediately, while 198.51.100.10 is gated on confirming it is not a sanctioned internal load test. The structural fixes (rate rule Count→Block, sensitive-path rule) are unaffected and remain the durable protection.
